notes: This page has no building step. It shows parts bag 1 (leads to the Uruk-hai catapult cart with 4 Uruk-hai) and bag 2 (leads to the Rohan wall with a horse rider and an archer), so no pieces were added.

Side note: the claude.ai Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive connectors need authorization through the claude.ai connector settings. They are unavailable until then. They weren't needed for this page.
No building step on this page. It only shows how to sort the parts: lay out loose bricks on a flat surface and open bag 1 without mixing it with bag 2. No pieces are added.

This page shows the assembly of one Uruk-hai minifigure: helmet, head, armour, torso with arms and hands, then legs. The minifigure parts (helmet, head, armour, torso, legs) are not in the parts list, so I did not record them as pieces.
The only listed part is the halberd (lego-6123), which the figure holds in its hand. I recorded it as b1 with no supporting piece. It has no joined partner because the hand is not a listed piece.
Only one figure is built on this page. The overview picture shows several Uruk-hai, but they are not recorded here.
I assumed the figure holds a halberd. The booklet shows it that way, and the parts list has two halberds.
The page shows three finished Uruk-hai minifigures. The left one holds the halberd (b1) already recorded on page 4, so it adds nothing new.
The other two figures each hold a shield (lego-10049) and a sword (lego-10050) in their hands. I recorded two shields and two swords, which matches the parts list quantities of 2 each.
The minifigure bodies are not in the parts list, so the weapons have no supporting pieces and no joins are recorded. The halberd, shields and swords are held in hands rather than clutched to bricks.
The second figure has long black hair instead of a helmet. The hair is not a listed part, so it is not recorded.
Step 1: the round 2x2 brick with axle hole (b7) is pressed onto one end of the black Technic plate 2x6 (b6).

Step 2 (2x): two black Technic 1x10 bricks (b8, b9) are laid across the plate, one at each side of the round brick, forming a U shape. I assumed they sit on the plate studs only, and do not touch the round brick or each other. The picture is ambiguous about exactly which studs of the plate they cover.

Step 3 (4x): four tan axle pins (lego-3749) are pushed into the end pin holes of the two Technic 1x10 bricks, two per brick. They stick out on the outer side as axle stubs for wheels later. The exact end holes (hole 1 and hole 9) are my reading of the picture.

Step 4: the black Technic plate 2x6 (b14) goes on the closed end of the U and covers the round brick (b7) as well as both Technic bricks. The dark bluish gray plate 2x6 (b15) goes on the opposite end across the same two bricks. The middle stays open.
The 'rests_on' for the plates is based on the picture: both plates bridge b8 and b9, and b14 also sits over b7. I cannot confirm from the picture that b14 touches b7's studs.

Step 5 (2x each): two reddish brown round 1x1 plates (b16, b17) go on the two far corner studs of the dark bluish gray plate b15. Two dark bluish gray brackets 1x2-2x2 (b18, b19) go on the black Technic plate b14 at the closed end, with their vertical faces and side studs facing outward.

Step 6 (4x): four curved 4x1 stud-less bricks (b20 to b23) form the fenders. I read their positions from the small picture: two over the bracket end and two on the other end plate b15. The exact studs they sit on are my estimate, so the rests_on lists may be slightly off.
Because the curved bricks are listed in the catalogue with stud ports only, I treated them as clutching from below onto the studs of the pieces named in rests_on.
Step 7 (4x): each of the four tan axle pins (b10 to b13) gets a black wheel, then a reddish brown round 2x2 plate with axle hole (lego-4032a) pushed on as a hub cap to hold it.

The black wheel tyres are not in the parts list, so they are not recorded as pieces. The hubs are recorded with no 'rests_on' because they clutch no studs. They connect only by the axle joins listed. These joins were assumed to let the wheel turn.

Step 8 (4x): four blue Technic half pins (lego-4274) go into pin holes in the sides of the two black Technic 1x10 bricks, two per brick. The pin hole numbers are estimates from the picture. These pins probably hold the catapult arm later.

Step 9 (2x): two reddish brown wood-grain 1x4 tiles (lego-2431pr0060) lie on top of the Technic bricks, one on each, between the fenders. I took them to be the wood-grain tiles rather than the plain 1x4 plates, because the strips look smooth and the plain plates are listed in a different count. Each tile covers four studs of its brick. The picture does not show which four, so rests_on is just the brick.

Step 10: a Technic axle 3 is pushed into each end of the reddish brown angled connector, which makes the catapult's pivot post. The sub-assembly is then pushed onto the chassis. The upper axle points up and the lower axle goes down into the cart's end.

Which end of the connector takes which axle is my assumption: the upper axle in the axle hole, the lower in the pin hole. The base join to the round brick b7 is also assumed, because the picture shows the post at the closed end of the chassis where b7 sits under the end plate. The post can turn.

Step 11: a small stack is built and put on the dark bluish gray end plate b15 of the cart: reddish brown round 2x2 plate (b37) at the bottom, black 45° 2x2 slope (b38) on it, and a reddish brown 1x2 plate (b39) on the two slope studs.

The slope's studs are on its high end, so the plate rests on both. I assume the round plate b37 covers studs of b15 not already used by the 1x1 round plates b16/b17. The picture is too small to confirm the exact studs.
This page starts a new, separate sub-assembly (shown at the top left as a finished piece to be added later). It is not yet attached to the chassis, so it has its own first piece.

Step 1: the black 1x6 plate (b40) is joined to the long side of the black wedge plate 3x6 (b41). The arrows show the plate moving to the wedge's edge, so I assumed the wedge's bottom clutches the 1x6's studs along one row. The picture could also be read as a side-by-side join, which is not possible with plates alone.
Step 2: the black 2x2 jumper plate with centre stud (b42) is pressed onto the middle of the wedge's top studs.
Step 3 (2x): two reddish brown round 1x1 plates (b43, b44) go on the wedge's studs, one at each side of the jumper plate.

Step 4: a reddish brown 1x4 plate (b45) is laid across the wedge near the jumper plate. I took it to be the plain Plate 1x4 (lego-3710) because the parts list still has two of them and the wood-grain tile is not shown here. Its rests_on lists the wedge and the jumper plate, which is my reading of the picture; the exact studs it covers are not certain.

Step 12: the finished wedge sub-assembly from pages 13 and 14 (b40 to b45) is turned on its side and pressed onto the outward-facing studs of the two brackets (b18, b19) at the closed end of the cart. This forms the standing back panel of the catapult.

No new pieces. I assumed the wedge plate b41 (not the 1x6 plate b40) is the piece that clutches the bracket side studs, and that it touches both brackets. The picture is small, so which piece sits on which stud is my best guess.
This page starts another new sub-assembly (shown at the top left of the page). It is not yet attached to the cart.

Step 1: the reddish brown sloped brick (b47) is pressed onto the studs of the dark bluish gray 4x4 inverted slope brick (b46). I identified it as the Brick Sloped Inverted 33° 3x2 (lego-3747b), the only matching reddish brown part left in the list.

Step 2: a reddish brown round 2x2 brick (b48) is pressed onto the studs at the other side of b46. I took it to be the Brick Round 2x2 with axle hole (lego-3941), because one is still unplaced. The exact studs used on b46 are my estimate.

Step 3 (4x): four dark bluish gray inverted brackets 1x2-1x2 (b49 to b52) are pressed onto the studs of the 4x4 inverted slope brick b46, side by side, with their upright faces toward the outside. Only one is shown being placed. I assumed four fill the 4x2 recess, going by the 4x box.

Step 4 (2x): two dark bluish gray Technic plates 2x4 (b53, b54) are laid on top of the brackets to make a flat 4x4 studded top. I picked the Technic plate lego-3709 because four are in the parts list and the plain lego-3020 plate is reddish brown. The pin-hole side faces the front.
The exact stud contacts (which bracket touches which plate) are my estimate from the small picture.

Step 5 (2x each): two black 1x1 plates with a horizontal clip (b55, b56) and two reddish brown 1x2 plates (b57, b58) are attached to the sides of the arm base. The booklet picture is small. I took the clip plates to be on the outer brackets b49 and b52, and the reddish plates on the middle brackets b50 and b51. This placement is a best guess.

Step 6 (2x): two black hinge tiles 1x3 (b59, b60) are fitted on the clip plates, one on each. Only one tile is shown being fitted, and the second is assumed from the 2x box. Each tile's finger points outward for the hinge connection later. The stud contacts for b59 and b60 are uncertain.

Step 7 (2x): each wing is built in three small steps: (1) a dark bluish gray hinge plate 1x2 (b61 / b64), (2) a reddish brown round 1x1 plate on one of its studs (b62 / b65), (3) a curved 4x1 brick on top (b63 / b66). The two wings are then hinged onto the black hinge tiles b59 and b60 of the arm base, one on each side, so they can swing.
The curved brick is assumed to clutch both the hinge plate and the round plate. The picture does not show exactly which studs are used.
Step 8: a black 1x2 30° slope (b68) is pressed onto the far end of a dark bluish gray 2x6 plate (b67). The plate is then placed on the arm base, so it sticks out as the long catapult arm.

The 2x6 plate overlaps the rear studs of the two Technic plates b53 and b54, so I listed both as supports. How many studs overlap is not clear in the picture. The slope's studs are on its high end, and I assumed it covers the last two studs of the plate.

Step 9: two black 1x8 grooved tiles (b69, b70) lie side by side along the long arm plate b67 and run back over the rear studs of the Technic plates b53/b54. A dark bluish gray Technic brick 1x2 (b71) is pressed onto the studs at the front of the base.

Step 10 (2x each): two black 1x3 bricks (b72, b73) are placed on the base next to the tiles. A black 33° 3x1 slope (b74, b75) is placed on top of each brick. I matched the pieces by colour and count from the parts list: black 3622 (2) and black 4286 (2).
All the stud contacts in this page are estimated from small drawings. In particular, which Technic plate (b53 or b54) each of b71, b72 and b73 sits on is a guess.

Step 11 is a small sub-assembly built in three steps. (1) The inverted bracket 1x2-1x2 (b76) is joined to the end of the light bluish gray plate 2x3 (b77). (2) The reddish brown plate 2x4 (b78) is laid on the plate. (3) The red 1x2 tile with handle (b79) goes on the exposed end. The finished piece is then placed at the free end of the arm.
The small pictures do not show exactly where the sub-assembly meets the arm. I assumed the bracket sits on the black slope b68 at the arm's end, which makes it the one connection to the arm.
Plate b78 and tile b79 are both assumed to sit on the plate b77, with b79 on the end that b78 leaves free.
Step 12 (2x): two dark bluish gray Technic plates 2x4 (b80, b81) are laid on the studs at the front of the arm base, making a flat 4x4 top. Which exact bricks each one sits on is an estimate.

Step 13 (2x): a grappling hook (lego-30192) is clipped on each side. I assumed they go into the two clips on the black clip plates (b55, b56). The picture shows them at the sides near the wing hinges, but the clips themselves are small in the drawing.

CORRECTION to page 13: the two silver curved pieces I recorded there as b82 and b83 with type lego-30192 (grappling hook) are in fact Wing / Blade 1x4 with Pin Hole (lego-98347, Flat Silver). The 98347 pieces are still in the unplaced list, and the real grappling hooks (30192) only appear on this page. Please read b82 and b83 as lego-98347 (Flat Silver). I could not change that earlier entry, so the clip joins b82-b55 and b83-b56 from page 13 are attached to the blades. The blades' own pin holes are used on this page.

Step 14 (2x): each copy is a grappling hook (b84 / b88) with a light bluish gray bush (b85 / b89) pushed onto its end, a reddish brown cone (b86 / b90) over the bush, and a light bluish gray pin with 2L bar (b87 / b91) as the stick. The finished stick-and-hook is then pushed into the pin hole of a blade (b82 / b83) at each side of the base.
How the bush, cone and stick fit together (bush on the hook's axle, cone over it, stick pin in the bush) is my reading of the small step pictures.
No building step on this page. It shows the safety warning (do not aim at the face) and how a finger pushes the bucket to launch the two hook-and-stick missiles from page 24. No pieces are added.
Reminder of my correction from page 24: b82 and b83 (recorded on page 13 as lego-30192) are really the Flat Silver Wing / Blade 1x4 pieces (lego-98347), and b84/b88 are the true grappling hooks.

Step 15: the finished catapult arm sub-assembly (built from page 16 on, with base b46) is lowered onto the upright axle b35 of the cart's pivot post. The axle goes into the axle hole of the reddish brown round brick b48 under the arm, so the arm can turn on the post.
No new pieces are added on this page.
Step 16 shows the finished bag 1 model: the catapult cart with four Uruk-hai minifigures. No new bricks are added.

The picture shows two figures holding halberds, but only one halberd (b1) was recorded earlier. The parts list has two, so I recorded the second halberd (b92) here. It is held in a minifigure hand, so it has no join to a brick. The minifigure bodies themselves are not in the parts list.
Figures in this picture: two with halberds, and two holding a shield and sword (b2-b5 from page 5).

Bag 2 starts here. The page shows two Rohan minifigures being assembled: a soldier with helmet, head, green cape, torso and legs, who holds a spear (b93) and a round Rohan shield (b94), and an archer who holds a bow (b95).

The minifigure parts (helmets, heads, cape, torsos, legs) are not in the parts list, so they are not recorded. The spear, shield and bow are held in hands, so no joins are recorded. The shield is carried in the hand, not on a clip I could see.
Step 1: the reddish brown horse with moveable legs (b96) is the base piece of this model.

Step 2: a reddish brown brick 1x2 (b97) is pressed onto the horse's back, and a reddish brown plate 1x2 (b98) goes on top of it. The inset shows a brick with a plate above it, and these are the only reddish brown 1x2 pieces left in the parts list. I assumed the brick connects to the horse's back by the horse's built-in connection and that the plate sits on the two brick studs.
Step 3: the dark bluish gray saddle with two clips (b99) is pressed onto the studs of the plate b98 on the horse's back, and the flat silver sword (b100) is held in one of the saddle's clips.

In the step 3 picture, a reddish brown brick is drawn loose at the lower left of the horse. I could not tell whether it is a spare or the brick b97 from page 29. I kept b97 and b98 as the saddle's support and recorded nothing for the loose brick.
Step 4: the Rohan rider minifigure is seated on the saddle with the spear (b93) and shield (b94) from page 28. The minifigure is not in the parts list, and nothing new is added for the rider's hands.

Step 1 (2x): two dark tan 6x8 plates (b101, b102) are placed side by side along their long edges to form the base of the wall model (shown at the top left). They are not clutched to each other by studs, so the join is only edge contact. Later bricks will bridge them.

Step 2: two dark bluish gray Technic bricks 1x2 (b103, b104) are placed at the two opposite ends of the base, with their pin holes facing outward. A dark bluish gray 2x3 brick (b105) is placed near the middle of the front edge.

The piece with six studs in the picture is the Brick 2x3 (dark bluish gray lego-3002), since the 2x4 bricks in the list are light bluish gray. Which of the two joined plates (b101 or b102) each brick rests on is estimated from the drawing.

Step 3 (2x each): at each end of the base, a light bluish gray brick 1x2 is placed next to the Technic brick and a Sand Green brick 1x3 next to it. This gives two gray-and-green runs, one on each of the two plates.
I used the Sand Green 1x3 (lego-3622) because the bright green bricks in the drawing match its listed colour. Which plate each pair sits on is estimated from the picture.

Step 4 (2x each): at each end of the base, a dark bluish gray 45° 2x1 slope with bottom pin (b110, b112) and a light bluish gray 2x2 wedged facet brick (b111, b113) are placed on the plate in front of the green bricks. They form the rocky outcrops at the foot of the wall.

I matched the shapes to the parts list: dark slope is lego-3040b and the pointed light gray brick is lego-87620. Which plate each brick sits on is estimated; the small bottom pin on b110 and b112 is not given any join.

Step 5: this layer is built on both ends of the wall base. The two Sand Green 1x3 bricks (b114, b116) go on the Technic bricks and gray 1x2 bricks at each end. The two light bluish gray corner bricks 2x2 (b115, b117) go over the first green runs. A light bluish gray 1x2 brick (b118) and a masonry-profile 1x2 brick (b119) finish the right-hand stack.

The small drawing leaves the exact stud contacts unclear, so each rests_on list is my best reading: the green and corner bricks sit on the end bricks and wedge bricks of the layer below. The right stack b117, b118, b119 is the most uncertain.

Step 6 (2x): a light bluish gray cheese slope 1x1 is pressed onto the side stud of a light bluish gray headlight brick 1x1. Then each headlight brick goes on top of a wall stack: one (b120) on the left corner brick b115, the other (b122) on the right 1x2 brick b118.
The slopes have no stud below them in this step, so they are only joined sideways. Which brick each headlight brick sits on is my estimate from the small picture.
Step 7: a dark bluish gray 45° 2x1 slope (b124) is placed on the middle dark 2x3 brick (b105). A light bluish gray brick 1x2 (b125) is placed on the base plate next to it, toward the left.
Their exact positions are estimated from the drawing, which shows them in the middle of the base between the two end stacks.
Step 8 (2x): two dark bluish gray steep 75° 2x1x3 slopes (b126, b127) are placed upright in the middle of the base, forming rocky pillars between the two end stacks.

I assumed both sit on the studs of the dark 2x3 brick b105. The 2x3 has six studs, enough for these two slopes plus the earlier small slope b124. The picture is small, so the exact studs are an estimate.

Step 9 (5x): five dark green 1x1 cheese slopes are pressed onto free studs around the rocks, as grass tufts: two on the left plate (b128, b129), one on the middle 2x3 brick (b130), and two on the right plate (b131, b132).
The grouping by plate is my best estimate from the small picture. Any of them could sit on a different plate or brick.

Step 10 (4x): four light bluish gray 1x1 bricks are used to make two two-brick columns, one at the far end of each green 1x3 run (b114 on the left, b116 on the right). The picture shows the left column being built and the right column already finished.
I assumed each column stands on the end stud of the green 1x3 brick on that side. That reading matches the 4x quantity.

Step 11 (2x each): a light bluish gray 1x4 brick and a Sand Green 1x1 brick are added at each end of the wall. The 1x4 bricks (b137, b139) run along the wall top. The green 1x1s (b138, b140) sit next to them.
I assumed each pair stands on the corner brick of that end (b115 on the left, b117 and b119 on the right). The exact studs covered are estimated from the small drawing.

Step 12: a light bluish gray 1x1 brick (b143) is pressed onto the hollow stud on top of the right tall 75° slope b127. Two more light bluish gray wedged 2x2 facet bricks (b141, b142) are added on top of the rock outcrops at each end, over the first wedges b111 and b113.
The wedge placement is estimated from the drawing, which shows a taller wedge group on the left. It may sit on other bricks next to b111 and b113. The 1x1 on the slope is clear from the arrow.

Step 13 (4x gray 1x2, 2x green 1x1): a new row goes on top of each of the two 1x4 bricks (b137 on the left, b139 on the right). Each side gets two light bluish gray 1x2 bricks with one Sand Green 1x1 between or beside them, as the picture shows.
I assumed the new bricks rest on the 1x4 brick of that side only. The columns of 1x1 bricks at the wall ends are unchanged.

Step 14: a Sand Green 1x1 brick (b150), two light bluish gray wedged 2x2 facet bricks (b151, b152) and one masonry 1x2 brick (b153) are added. The wedges go on top of the earlier wedges b141 and b142, making two taller rock columns. The masonry brick goes on the right column and the green brick goes on the left one.
The picture's third icon matches the masonry-profile brick lego-98283, because four are still in the unplaced list. The placement of each part is a best guess from the small isometric picture.

Step 15: a light bluish gray 1x2x2 panel (b156) is lowered onto the middle of the wall over the 1x1 brick b143 and the wedge b152. A light bluish gray 1x3 arch brick (b154, b155) is placed on the top of each end tower, giving arched windows.
Which studs each piece sits on is estimated from the small drawing. The arch bricks are the 2x icon, one for each end of the wall, and the panel is the single piece in the callout.
Step 16: a light bluish gray 1x4 brick is added on top of each end of the wall (b157 on the left, b158 on the right). A Sand Green 1x1 brick (b159) is pressed onto a stud of the middle panel b156.
The stud contacts are estimated from the drawing: each 1x4 sits on the two 1x2 bricks of the row below on its side.

Step 17 (2x): for each of two copies, a light bluish gray cheese slope 1x1 is pressed onto the side stud of a light bluish gray headlight brick 1x1. One copy (b160 + b161) goes on the left wedge column of the wall, and the other (b162 + b163) on the right column.
Positions are estimated from the two small insets and the main picture. The left one sits on b151 and the right one on the masonry brick b153.

Step 18: a light bluish gray 1x6 brick (b164) is laid across the middle of the wall. It bridges the headlight brick b160 on the left column, the panel b156 in the middle, and the headlight brick b162 on the right column, so it ties the structure together.
The brick's exact stud contacts are estimated. The green 1x1 b159 next to it is left uncovered in the picture.
The wall model is turned over. Step 19 builds a T-shaped dark reddish brown path from two pieces (step 1 and step 2) and lays it on the tan base plates at the front of the wall's gate opening.

The two reddish brown pieces left in the unplaced list are the Plate 1x4 (lego-3710) and the wood-grain Tile 1x4 (lego-2431pr0060). I used them as the two pieces. The drawing shows studs on the T, which would not match a tile, so this identification is uncertain. Their positions over both base plates (b101, b102) are also estimated.

Step 20: the wall is seen from behind. A dark red 1x2 grooved tile (b167) is placed on the top corner of the left tower, and a light bluish gray masonry 1x2 brick (b168) is added next to it on the same row. The tile is the only dark red piece left in the unplaced list.
I assumed both sit on the 1x4 brick b157 at the top of the left tower. The first reddish icon looks like a small plate, but the dark red tile is the matching unplaced piece.
Step 21: a dark bluish gray round 1x1 plate (b169) is pressed onto the dark red piece at the top-left corner of the left tower.

The arrow lands on the dark red piece (b167), so I recorded b167 as the support. A grooved tile has no studs, so the round plate may really clutch the stud of the tower brick next to the dark red piece. I could not tell which from the drawing.

Step 22: the reddish brown 7x4x6 stairs (b170) go against the back of the left tower. The bottom end rests on the reddish brown path pieces (b165, b166) and the top end on the tower's top brick (b157).
Stud contacts are estimated from the picture. The stairs are drawn at a slant along the wall, so the exact studs they clutch are not clear.
Step 23: a reddish brown 1x4 plate (b171) is pressed onto the top end of the stairs, where they meet the tower, finishing the landing.

Parts-count warning: by my earlier records both lego-3710 plates (b45, b165) are already used, so no Plate 1x4 should be left. The unplaced list shows no reddish brown 1x4 plate either. One of my earlier identifications (for example b45 on page 14, or b165/b166 on page 49) is probably wrong. I recorded this piece as lego-3710 as the best match for the picture.

Step 24 (1x brick 2x4, 2x wedge): a light bluish gray 2x4 brick (b172) is placed on top of the long 1x6 beam b164 over the gate. Two light bluish gray wedged 2x2 facet bricks (b173, b174) go next to it on the same beam, making the roof of the gateway.
The wedge icon here matches lego-87620 (four are left in the unplaced list). The exact studs of b164 used by each piece are estimated, since b164 is only six studs long.

Step 25 (2x each): two light bluish gray 2x4 bricks (b175, b176) cover the top of the wall on each side of the gate roof, bridging the 1x4 tower brick and the 1x6 beam b164. Two Sand Green 1x1 bricks (b177, b178) are placed on the right tower and near the gate for colour accents.
The stud contacts are estimated from the picture. The Sand Green 1x1 count in the unplaced list may be out of step with my records; I used the colour shown in the picture.

Step 26: two light bluish gray 2x16 plates (b179, b180) are laid side by side along the top of the wall as the walkway. A light bluish gray 1x6 plate (b181) is then pressed on top, spanning both plates.

The stud contacts of the long plates are estimated: both are assumed to bridge the 2x4 bricks and the gate-roof bricks below. The 1x6 plate sits across the seam of the two long plates, so it clutches both.
Step 27: the first bricks of the parapet are added to the walkway: a 1x4 brick (b182) at the back left, a 1x2 brick (b183) next to it, and a masonry 1x2 brick (b184) near the right end.
I assumed the 1x4 and 1x2 sit on the back plate b179 and the masonry brick on the front plate b180. The picture is too small to read the positions closely.
Step 28: the back parapet of the walkway is extended with a light bluish gray 1x2 brick (b185), two wedged 2x2 facet bricks (b186, b187) and a masonry 1x2 brick (b188).

The two wedges match the last two lego-87620 in the unplaced list, and the masonry brick is the next-to-last lego-98283. I assumed the first three sit on the back plate b179 and the masonry brick on the front plate b180. This is estimated from the picture.

Step 29: four dark bluish gray jumper plates 1x2 (b189 to b192) are placed in the middle of the walkway, forming a dark patch where the archer will stand. Two dark bluish gray 45° 2x1 slopes with bottom pin (b193, b194) are added at the walkway corners: one at the front right and one at the back left.
The jumper plates are only drawn in the middle of the walkway. Which of the long plates each one covers is my estimate, since the middle ones probably cross the seam between b179 and b180.

Step 30 (2x jumper, 6x brick 1x2, 1x slope): the back parapet gets two dark jumper plates (b195, b196) at the back-left, six light bluish gray 1x2 bricks (b197 to b202) along the back and right parts, and a light bluish gray 30° 1x2 slope (b203) at the front right.
Which of the long plates each piece sits on is estimated. Four bricks are put on the back plate and two on the front plate, as the picture suggests. Please treat the splits as approximate.
Step 31 (6x): a light bluish gray 30° 1x2 slope is pressed on top of each of the six 1x2 parapet bricks placed on page 60 (b197 to b202), making the sloped crenellations of the wall.
The one-to-one pairing of slope and brick is my reading of the picture. The slopes cover the bricks' studs.

This page starts a new sub-assembly, the small swinging launcher mounted on a base. Step 1: the long tan pin goes into a black pin connector plate (b213). Step 2: the pin passes through the pin hole of the dark brown launcher (b211), which is the black-looking catapult piece in the picture. Step 3: the second pin connector plate (b214) closes the other end of the pin. Step 4: the two connector plates are pressed on the studs of a reddish brown 2x3 brick (b212).

The 'black' pieces in the pictures look black but I matched them to the unplaced list: the Launcher (lego-88289, Dark Brown) and the Technic Pin Connector Plates (lego-32530, Black). The reddish brown 2x3 brick (lego-3002) is recorded here as a new piece because I have not placed it before.
The launcher does not rest on any stud, since it swings on the pin between the two connector plates.

The launcher sub-assembly from page 62 (base b212) is placed on the walkway at the patch of dark jumper plates. No new pieces are added. The base b212 is now clutched to the jumper plates b189 to b192 and the walkway plates below, so I am adding that placement as a note rather than a new piece.

Because the schema only lets me list rests_on on newly placed pieces, I cannot add rests_on to b212, which was recorded on page 62 with an empty list. The intended contacts are: b212 rests on b189, b190, b191 and b192.

Step 33 (3x): three dark bluish gray round 1x1 bricks with open studs are placed on the front walkway plate b180 beside the launcher as ammunition. The picture shows two of them clearly, with the third assumed from the 3x box. The finger shows how the launcher is pushed to fire them, and the warning symbol says not to aim at faces.
Their exact studs on b180 are not specified. They are loose ammunition, so they simply sit on studs.

Step 34: a flagpole is built from a reddish brown cone (b218), a reddish brown 6L bar (b219) pushed into it, and two flags (b220 Pearl Gold, b221 Dark Green) slid onto the bar. The pole is then planted on the left tower, on the dark bluish gray round plate b169 at the top corner.
At the right tower top, a torch support (b222, Dark Brown, shown as black) is put on the green 1x1 brick b177. A trans-neon orange flame (b223) is pushed into it.

The page is shown from the front of the wall, so the model has been turned around. The positions on the towers are my reading: the flagpole at the left tower's top corner and the torch at the right tower's top.

Step 35 (2x): two black Technic pins with friction ridges (b224, b225) are pushed into the pin holes of the two Technic 1x2 bricks at the ends of the wall base (b103 on the left, b104 on the right). Only the left end is shown in the picture, and the right is assumed from the 2x box.
These pins are probably used later to hold extra pieces at the ends of the wall.

This page shows the finished bag 2 model: the Rohan wall with the archer standing on the walkway and the horse rider next to it. No new pieces are added. The minifigure bodies are not in the parts list.

Unplaced pieces still in the list: 4x lego-60474 round 4x4 plates, 1x lego-87079 tile 2x4 and 2x lego-98347 blades. They may be used on the following pages, for example the round plates under the wheels of the second set of models.

Reminder of my earlier mix-up: b82 and b83 on page 13 were recorded as lego-30192, but they should be lego-98347 (Flat Silver blades). That would leave the two blades placed and the true grappling hooks as b84 and b88 only.
No building step on this page. It is a checklist of other Lord of the Rings minifigures from other sets, such as Frodo, Gandalf, Eomer and Gimli, so nothing is added.

No building step on this page. It continues the checklist of other Lord of the Rings minifigures and creatures (Aragorn, Legolas, Cave Troll, King Theoden and others) from other sets, so nothing is added.
No building step on this page. It advertises set 9474 (The Battle of Helm's Deep) and shows how this set (9471) can be combined with it. Nothing is added.

No building step on this page. It is an advertisement for The Hobbit: An Unexpected Journey, so nothing is added.
No building step on this page. It is the back cover with a survey competition advertisement, so nothing is added.

Final summary of known issues: (1) b82 and b83 (page 13) should be lego-98347 Flat Silver blades, not lego-30192. The 30192 hooks are b84 and b88 only. (2) Four lego-60474 round plates, one lego-87079 tile and two lego-98347 blades never appeared in any step I could identify, so they are unplaced. If b82 and b83 are corrected to 98347, the 98347 pieces are placed and only the round plates and the tile remain. (3) The minifigure bodies (heads, torsos, legs, helmets) and the tyres are not in the parts list, so they are not recorded. (4) Many stud contacts were estimated from small isometric pictures.

Real problem fixed (b169): a tile has no studs, so b169 cannot rest on the grooved tile b167. The earlier entry for b169 stays as given, but its real support is a stud of the masonry brick b168 on the same 1x4 brick b157. I added that join. Please treat the old b169-on-b167 support as wrong.

Real problem fixed (b170): b166 is the wood-grain tile and has no studs, so it cannot support the stairs b170. The stairs really clutch the studded plate b165 and the tower brick b157. I added the b170-b165 join. Please treat b166 as not supporting b170.

Real problem fixed (separate group): the launcher sub-assembly (b210 to b214) had no link to the wall, because b212 was recorded with an empty rests_on on page 62 and page 63 added no pieces. I added joins from b212 to the jumper plates b189 to b192 it is pressed onto.

Separate groups that are real and kept: (1) the catapult cart with its arm and (2) the Rohan wall are two different models in the booklet. They are not attached to each other. The horse with saddle and sword (b96 to b100) is a third model.

I linked the rider's spear and shield (b93, b94) to the saddle and the archer's bow (b95) to the walkway, as loose contact edges. They are held by minifigures, which are not in the parts list. The Uruk-hai halberds, swords and shields (b1 to b5, b92) are also held by minifigures standing beside the cart, so they have no brick to join and stay as separate pieces. This is expected, not a mistake.

Still open from earlier pages: b82 and b83 should be lego-98347 (Flat Silver blades), not lego-30192. The 4x lego-60474 round plates and the 1x lego-87079 tile are not used in any step I could identify.

Corrected entries for b169 and b170: these two ids replace the earlier entries of the same ids, with a fixed rests_on. b169 (round 1x1 plate) now rests on the masonry brick b168, which has studs. It no longer rests on the grooved tile b167. b170 (stairs) now rests on the studded plate b165 and the tower brick b157. It no longer rests on the wood-grain tile b166, which has no studs.
The earlier joins b169-b168 and b170-b165 still apply, and agree with this.

Remaining separate groups, kept on purpose: the Uruk-hai weapons held by minifigures (halberds b1 and b92, and the sword and shield pairs b2/b3 and b4/b5). These are held by minifigures, which are not in the parts list, and the figures only stand next to the cart without touching it. Linking them to the cart would invent a physical connection that the booklet does not show. The catapult cart with its arm, the Rohan wall with its launcher, and the horse with saddle are separate models in the booklet.

notes: This page has no building step. It shows parts bag 1 (leads to the Uruk-hai catapult cart with 4 Uruk-hai) and bag 2 (leads to the Rohan wall with a horse rider and an archer), so no pieces were added.

Side note: the claude.ai Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive connectors need authorization through the claude.ai connector settings. They are unavailable until then. They weren't needed for this page.
No building step on this page. It only shows how to sort the parts: lay out loose bricks on a flat surface and open bag 1 without mixing it with bag 2. No pieces are added.

This page shows the assembly of one Uruk-hai minifigure: helmet, head, armour, torso with arms and hands, then legs. The minifigure parts (helmet, head, armour, torso, legs) are not in the parts list, so I did not record them as pieces.
The only listed part is the halberd (lego-6123), which the figure holds in its hand. I recorded it as b1 with no supporting piece. It has no joined partner because the hand is not a listed piece.
Only one figure is built on this page. The overview picture shows several Uruk-hai, but they are not recorded here.
I assumed the figure holds a halberd. The booklet shows it that way, and the parts list has two halberds.
The page shows three finished Uruk-hai minifigures. The left one holds the halberd (b1) already recorded on page 4, so it adds nothing new.
The other two figures each hold a shield (lego-10049) and a sword (lego-10050) in their hands. I recorded two shields and two swords, which matches the parts list quantities of 2 each.
The minifigure bodies are not in the parts list, so the weapons have no supporting pieces and no joins are recorded. The halberd, shields and swords are held in hands rather than clutched to bricks.
The second figure has long black hair instead of a helmet. The hair is not a listed part, so it is not recorded.
Step 1: the round 2x2 brick with axle hole (b7) is pressed onto one end of the black Technic plate 2x6 (b6).

Step 2 (2x): two black Technic 1x10 bricks (b8, b9) are laid across the plate, one at each side of the round brick, forming a U shape. I assumed they sit on the plate studs only, and do not touch the round brick or each other. The picture is ambiguous about exactly which studs of the plate they cover.

Step 3 (4x): four tan axle pins (lego-3749) are pushed into the end pin holes of the two Technic 1x10 bricks, two per brick. They stick out on the outer side as axle stubs for wheels later. The exact end holes (hole 1 and hole 9) are my reading of the picture.

Step 4: the black Technic plate 2x6 (b14) goes on the closed end of the U and covers the round brick (b7) as well as both Technic bricks. The dark bluish gray plate 2x6 (b15) goes on the opposite end across the same two bricks. The middle stays open.
The 'rests_on' for the plates is based on the picture: both plates bridge b8 and b9, and b14 also sits over b7. I cannot confirm from the picture that b14 touches b7's studs.

Step 5 (2x each): two reddish brown round 1x1 plates (b16, b17) go on the two far corner studs of the dark bluish gray plate b15. Two dark bluish gray brackets 1x2-2x2 (b18, b19) go on the black Technic plate b14 at the closed end, with their vertical faces and side studs facing outward.

Step 6 (4x): four curved 4x1 stud-less bricks (b20 to b23) form the fenders. I read their positions from the small picture: two over the bracket end and two on the other end plate b15. The exact studs they sit on are my estimate, so the rests_on lists may be slightly off.
Because the curved bricks are listed in the catalogue with stud ports only, I treated them as clutching from below onto the studs of the pieces named in rests_on.
Step 7 (4x): each of the four tan axle pins (b10 to b13) gets a black wheel, then a reddish brown round 2x2 plate with axle hole (lego-4032a) pushed on as a hub cap to hold it.

The black wheel tyres are not in the parts list, so they are not recorded as pieces. The hubs are recorded with no 'rests_on' because they clutch no studs. They connect only by the axle joins listed. These joins were assumed to let the wheel turn.

Step 8 (4x): four blue Technic half pins (lego-4274) go into pin holes in the sides of the two black Technic 1x10 bricks, two per brick. The pin hole numbers are estimates from the picture. These pins probably hold the catapult arm later.

Step 9 (2x): two reddish brown wood-grain 1x4 tiles (lego-2431pr0060) lie on top of the Technic bricks, one on each, between the fenders. I took them to be the wood-grain tiles rather than the plain 1x4 plates, because the strips look smooth and the plain plates are listed in a different count. Each tile covers four studs of its brick. The picture does not show which four, so rests_on is just the brick.

Step 10: a Technic axle 3 is pushed into each end of the reddish brown angled connector, which makes the catapult's pivot post. The sub-assembly is then pushed onto the chassis. The upper axle points up and the lower axle goes down into the cart's end.

Which end of the connector takes which axle is my assumption: the upper axle in the axle hole, the lower in the pin hole. The base join to the round brick b7 is also assumed, because the picture shows the post at the closed end of the chassis where b7 sits under the end plate. The post can turn.

Step 11: a small stack is built and put on the dark bluish gray end plate b15 of the cart: reddish brown round 2x2 plate (b37) at the bottom, black 45° 2x2 slope (b38) on it, and a reddish brown 1x2 plate (b39) on the two slope studs.

The slope's studs are on its high end, so the plate rests on both. I assume the round plate b37 covers studs of b15 not already used by the 1x1 round plates b16/b17. The picture is too small to confirm the exact studs.
This page starts a new, separate sub-assembly (shown at the top left as a finished piece to be added later). It is not yet attached to the chassis, so it has its own first piece.

Step 1: the black 1x6 plate (b40) is joined to the long side of the black wedge plate 3x6 (b41). The arrows show the plate moving to the wedge's edge, so I assumed the wedge's bottom clutches the 1x6's studs along one row. The picture could also be read as a side-by-side join, which is not possible with plates alone.
Step 2: the black 2x2 jumper plate with centre stud (b42) is pressed onto the middle of the wedge's top studs.
Step 3 (2x): two reddish brown round 1x1 plates (b43, b44) go on the wedge's studs, one at each side of the jumper plate.

Step 4: a reddish brown 1x4 plate (b45) is laid across the wedge near the jumper plate. I took it to be the plain Plate 1x4 (lego-3710) because the parts list still has two of them and the wood-grain tile is not shown here. Its rests_on lists the wedge and the jumper plate, which is my reading of the picture; the exact studs it covers are not certain.

Step 12: the finished wedge sub-assembly from pages 13 and 14 (b40 to b45) is turned on its side and pressed onto the outward-facing studs of the two brackets (b18, b19) at the closed end of the cart. This forms the standing back panel of the catapult.

No new pieces. I assumed the wedge plate b41 (not the 1x6 plate b40) is the piece that clutches the bracket side studs, and that it touches both brackets. The picture is small, so which piece sits on which stud is my best guess.
This page starts another new sub-assembly (shown at the top left of the page). It is not yet attached to the cart.

Step 1: the reddish brown sloped brick (b47) is pressed onto the studs of the dark bluish gray 4x4 inverted slope brick (b46). I identified it as the Brick Sloped Inverted 33° 3x2 (lego-3747b), the only matching reddish brown part left in the list.

Step 2: a reddish brown round 2x2 brick (b48) is pressed onto the studs at the other side of b46. I took it to be the Brick Round 2x2 with axle hole (lego-3941), because one is still unplaced. The exact studs used on b46 are my estimate.

Step 3 (4x): four dark bluish gray inverted brackets 1x2-1x2 (b49 to b52) are pressed onto the studs of the 4x4 inverted slope brick b46, side by side, with their upright faces toward the outside. Only one is shown being placed. I assumed four fill the 4x2 recess, going by the 4x box.

Step 4 (2x): two dark bluish gray Technic plates 2x4 (b53, b54) are laid on top of the brackets to make a flat 4x4 studded top. I picked the Technic plate lego-3709 because four are in the parts list and the plain lego-3020 plate is reddish brown. The pin-hole side faces the front.
The exact stud contacts (which bracket touches which plate) are my estimate from the small picture.

Step 5 (2x each): two black 1x1 plates with a horizontal clip (b55, b56) and two reddish brown 1x2 plates (b57, b58) are attached to the sides of the arm base. The booklet picture is small. I took the clip plates to be on the outer brackets b49 and b52, and the reddish plates on the middle brackets b50 and b51. This placement is a best guess.

Step 6 (2x): two black hinge tiles 1x3 (b59, b60) are fitted on the clip plates, one on each. Only one tile is shown being fitted, and the second is assumed from the 2x box. Each tile's finger points outward for the hinge connection later. The stud contacts for b59 and b60 are uncertain.

Step 7 (2x): each wing is built in three small steps: (1) a dark bluish gray hinge plate 1x2 (b61 / b64), (2) a reddish brown round 1x1 plate on one of its studs (b62 / b65), (3) a curved 4x1 brick on top (b63 / b66). The two wings are then hinged onto the black hinge tiles b59 and b60 of the arm base, one on each side, so they can swing.
The curved brick is assumed to clutch both the hinge plate and the round plate. The picture does not show exactly which studs are used.
Step 8: a black 1x2 30° slope (b68) is pressed onto the far end of a dark bluish gray 2x6 plate (b67). The plate is then placed on the arm base, so it sticks out as the long catapult arm.

The 2x6 plate overlaps the rear studs of the two Technic plates b53 and b54, so I listed both as supports. How many studs overlap is not clear in the picture. The slope's studs are on its high end, and I assumed it covers the last two studs of the plate.

Step 9: two black 1x8 grooved tiles (b69, b70) lie side by side along the long arm plate b67 and run back over the rear studs of the Technic plates b53/b54. A dark bluish gray Technic brick 1x2 (b71) is pressed onto the studs at the front of the base.

Step 10 (2x each): two black 1x3 bricks (b72, b73) are placed on the base next to the tiles. A black 33° 3x1 slope (b74, b75) is placed on top of each brick. I matched the pieces by colour and count from the parts list: black 3622 (2) and black 4286 (2).
All the stud contacts in this page are estimated from small drawings. In particular, which Technic plate (b53 or b54) each of b71, b72 and b73 sits on is a guess.

Step 11 is a small sub-assembly built in three steps. (1) The inverted bracket 1x2-1x2 (b76) is joined to the end of the light bluish gray plate 2x3 (b77). (2) The reddish brown plate 2x4 (b78) is laid on the plate. (3) The red 1x2 tile with handle (b79) goes on the exposed end. The finished piece is then placed at the free end of the arm.
The small pictures do not show exactly where the sub-assembly meets the arm. I assumed the bracket sits on the black slope b68 at the arm's end, which makes it the one connection to the arm.
Plate b78 and tile b79 are both assumed to sit on the plate b77, with b79 on the end that b78 leaves free.
Step 12 (2x): two dark bluish gray Technic plates 2x4 (b80, b81) are laid on the studs at the front of the arm base, making a flat 4x4 top. Which exact bricks each one sits on is an estimate.

Step 13 (2x): a grappling hook (lego-30192) is clipped on each side. I assumed they go into the two clips on the black clip plates (b55, b56). The picture shows them at the sides near the wing hinges, but the clips themselves are small in the drawing.

CORRECTION to page 13: the two silver curved pieces I recorded there as b82 and b83 with type lego-30192 (grappling hook) are in fact Wing / Blade 1x4 with Pin Hole (lego-98347, Flat Silver). The 98347 pieces are still in the unplaced list, and the real grappling hooks (30192) only appear on this page. Please read b82 and b83 as lego-98347 (Flat Silver). I could not change that earlier entry, so the clip joins b82-b55 and b83-b56 from page 13 are attached to the blades. The blades' own pin holes are used on this page.

Step 14 (2x): each copy is a grappling hook (b84 / b88) with a light bluish gray bush (b85 / b89) pushed onto its end, a reddish brown cone (b86 / b90) over the bush, and a light bluish gray pin with 2L bar (b87 / b91) as the stick. The finished stick-and-hook is then pushed into the pin hole of a blade (b82 / b83) at each side of the base.
How the bush, cone and stick fit together (bush on the hook's axle, cone over it, stick pin in the bush) is my reading of the small step pictures.
No building step on this page. It shows the safety warning (do not aim at the face) and how a finger pushes the bucket to launch the two hook-and-stick missiles from page 24. No pieces are added.
Reminder of my correction from page 24: b82 and b83 (recorded on page 13 as lego-30192) are really the Flat Silver Wing / Blade 1x4 pieces (lego-98347), and b84/b88 are the true grappling hooks.

Step 15: the finished catapult arm sub-assembly (built from page 16 on, with base b46) is lowered onto the upright axle b35 of the cart's pivot post. The axle goes into the axle hole of the reddish brown round brick b48 under the arm, so the arm can turn on the post.
No new pieces are added on this page.
Step 16 shows the finished bag 1 model: the catapult cart with four Uruk-hai minifigures. No new bricks are added.

The picture shows two figures holding halberds, but only one halberd (b1) was recorded earlier. The parts list has two, so I recorded the second halberd (b92) here. It is held in a minifigure hand, so it has no join to a brick. The minifigure bodies themselves are not in the parts list.
Figures in this picture: two with halberds, and two holding a shield and sword (b2-b5 from page 5).

Bag 2 starts here. The page shows two Rohan minifigures being assembled: a soldier with helmet, head, green cape, torso and legs, who holds a spear (b93) and a round Rohan shield (b94), and an archer who holds a bow (b95).

The minifigure parts (helmets, heads, cape, torsos, legs) are not in the parts list, so they are not recorded. The spear, shield and bow are held in hands, so no joins are recorded. The shield is carried in the hand, not on a clip I could see.
Step 1: the reddish brown horse with moveable legs (b96) is the base piece of this model.

Step 2: a reddish brown brick 1x2 (b97) is pressed onto the horse's back, and a reddish brown plate 1x2 (b98) goes on top of it. The inset shows a brick with a plate above it, and these are the only reddish brown 1x2 pieces left in the parts list. I assumed the brick connects to the horse's back by the horse's built-in connection and that the plate sits on the two brick studs.
Step 3: the dark bluish gray saddle with two clips (b99) is pressed onto the studs of the plate b98 on the horse's back, and the flat silver sword (b100) is held in one of the saddle's clips.

In the step 3 picture, a reddish brown brick is drawn loose at the lower left of the horse. I could not tell whether it is a spare or the brick b97 from page 29. I kept b97 and b98 as the saddle's support and recorded nothing for the loose brick.
Step 4: the Rohan rider minifigure is seated on the saddle with the spear (b93) and shield (b94) from page 28. The minifigure is not in the parts list, and nothing new is added for the rider's hands.

Step 1 (2x): two dark tan 6x8 plates (b101, b102) are placed side by side along their long edges to form the base of the wall model (shown at the top left). They are not clutched to each other by studs, so the join is only edge contact. Later bricks will bridge them.

I used the Sand Green 1x3 (lego-3622) because the bright green bricks in the drawing match its listed colour. Which plate each pair sits on is estimated from the picture.

Step 4 (2x each): at each end of the base, a dark bluish gray 45° 2x1 slope with bottom pin (b110, b112) and a light bluish gray 2x2 wedged facet brick (b111, b113) are placed on the plate in front of the green bricks. They form the rocky outcrops at the foot of the wall.

I matched the shapes to the parts list: dark slope is lego-3040b and the pointed light gray brick is lego-87620. Which plate each brick sits on is estimated; the small bottom pin on b110 and b112 is not given any join.

Step 5: this layer is built on both ends of the wall base. The two Sand Green 1x3 bricks (b114, b116) go on the Technic bricks and gray 1x2 bricks at each end. The two light bluish gray corner bricks 2x2 (b115, b117) go over the first green runs. A light bluish gray 1x2 brick (b118) and a masonry-profile 1x2 brick (b119) finish the right-hand stack.

The small drawing leaves the exact stud contacts unclear, so each rests_on list is my best reading: the green and corner bricks sit on the end bricks and wedge bricks of the layer below. The right stack b117, b118, b119 is the most uncertain.

Step 6 (2x): a light bluish gray cheese slope 1x1 is pressed onto the side stud of a light bluish gray headlight brick 1x1. Then each headlight brick goes on top of a wall stack: one (b120) on the left corner brick b115, the other (b122) on the right 1x2 brick b118.
The slopes have no stud below them in this step, so they are only joined sideways. Which brick each headlight brick sits on is my estimate from the small picture.
Step 7: a dark bluish gray 45° 2x1 slope (b124) is placed on the middle dark 2x3 brick (b105). A light bluish gray brick 1x2 (b125) is placed on the base plate next to it, toward the left.
Their exact positions are estimated from the drawing, which shows them in the middle of the base between the two end stacks.
Step 8 (2x): two dark bluish gray steep 75° 2x1x3 slopes (b126, b127) are placed upright in the middle of the base, forming rocky pillars between the two end stacks.

I assumed both sit on the studs of the dark 2x3 brick b105. The 2x3 has six studs, enough for these two slopes plus the earlier small slope b124. The picture is small, so the exact studs are an estimate.

Step 9 (5x): five dark green 1x1 cheese slopes are pressed onto free studs around the rocks, as grass tufts: two on the left plate (b128, b129), one on the middle 2x3 brick (b130), and two on the right plate (b131, b132).
The grouping by plate is my best estimate from the small picture. Any of them could sit on a different plate or brick.

Step 10 (4x): four light bluish gray 1x1 bricks are used to make two two-brick columns, one at the far end of each green 1x3 run (b114 on the left, b116 on the right). The picture shows the left column being built and the right column already finished.
I assumed each column stands on the end stud of the green 1x3 brick on that side. That reading matches the 4x quantity.

Step 11 (2x each): a light bluish gray 1x4 brick and a Sand Green 1x1 brick are added at each end of the wall. The 1x4 bricks (b137, b139) run along the wall top. The green 1x1s (b138, b140) sit next to them.
I assumed each pair stands on the corner brick of that end (b115 on the left, b117 and b119 on the right). The exact studs covered are estimated from the small drawing.

Step 12: a light bluish gray 1x1 brick (b143) is pressed onto the hollow stud on top of the right tall 75° slope b127. Two more light bluish gray wedged 2x2 facet bricks (b141, b142) are added on top of the rock outcrops at each end, over the first wedges b111 and b113.
The wedge placement is estimated from the drawing, which shows a taller wedge group on the left. It may sit on other bricks next to b111 and b113. The 1x1 on the slope is clear from the arrow.

Step 13 (4x gray 1x2, 2x green 1x1): a new row goes on top of each of the two 1x4 bricks (b137 on the left, b139 on the right). Each side gets two light bluish gray 1x2 bricks with one Sand Green 1x1 between or beside them, as the picture shows.
I assumed the new bricks rest on the 1x4 brick of that side only. The columns of 1x1 bricks at the wall ends are unchanged.

Step 14: a Sand Green 1x1 brick (b150), two light bluish gray wedged 2x2 facet bricks (b151, b152) and one masonry 1x2 brick (b153) are added. The wedges go on top of the earlier wedges b141 and b142, making two taller rock columns. The masonry brick goes on the right column and the green brick goes on the left one.
The picture's third icon matches the masonry-profile brick lego-98283, because four are still in the unplaced list. The placement of each part is a best guess from the small isometric picture.

Step 15: a light bluish gray 1x2x2 panel (b156) is lowered onto the middle of the wall over the 1x1 brick b143 and the wedge b152. A light bluish gray 1x3 arch brick (b154, b155) is placed on the top of each end tower, giving arched windows.
Which studs each piece sits on is estimated from the small drawing. The arch bricks are the 2x icon, one for each end of the wall, and the panel is the single piece in the callout.
Step 16: a light bluish gray 1x4 brick is added on top of each end of the wall (b157 on the left, b158 on the right). A Sand Green 1x1 brick (b159) is pressed onto a stud of the middle panel b156.
The stud contacts are estimated from the drawing: each 1x4 sits on the two 1x2 bricks of the row below on its side.

Step 17 (2x): for each of two copies, a light bluish gray cheese slope 1x1 is pressed onto the side stud of a light bluish gray headlight brick 1x1. One copy (b160 + b161) goes on the left wedge column of the wall, and the other (b162 + b163) on the right column.
Positions are estimated from the two small insets and the main picture. The left one sits on b151 and the right one on the masonry brick b153.

Step 18: a light bluish gray 1x6 brick (b164) is laid across the middle of the wall. It bridges the headlight brick b160 on the left column, the panel b156 in the middle, and the headlight brick b162 on the right column, so it ties the structure together.
The brick's exact stud contacts are estimated. The green 1x1 b159 next to it is left uncovered in the picture.
The wall model is turned over. Step 19 builds a T-shaped dark reddish brown path from two pieces (step 1 and step 2) and lays it on the tan base plates at the front of the wall's gate opening.

The two reddish brown pieces left in the unplaced list are the Plate 1x4 (lego-3710) and the wood-grain Tile 1x4 (lego-2431pr0060). I used them as the two pieces. The drawing shows studs on the T, which would not match a tile, so this identification is uncertain. Their positions over both base plates (b101, b102) are also estimated.

Step 20: the wall is seen from behind. A dark red 1x2 grooved tile (b167) is placed on the top corner of the left tower, and a light bluish gray masonry 1x2 brick (b168) is added next to it on the same row. The tile is the only dark red piece left in the unplaced list.
I assumed both sit on the 1x4 brick b157 at the top of the left tower. The first reddish icon looks like a small plate, but the dark red tile is the matching unplaced piece.
Step 21: a dark bluish gray round 1x1 plate (b169) is pressed onto the dark red piece at the top-left corner of the left tower.

The arrow lands on the dark red piece (b167), so I recorded b167 as the support. A grooved tile has no studs, so the round plate may really clutch the stud of the tower brick next to the dark red piece. I could not tell which from the drawing.

Step 22: the reddish brown 7x4x6 stairs (b170) go against the back of the left tower. The bottom end rests on the reddish brown path pieces (b165, b166) and the top end on the tower's top brick (b157).
Stud contacts are estimated from the picture. The stairs are drawn at a slant along the wall, so the exact studs they clutch are not clear.
Step 23: a reddish brown 1x4 plate (b171) is pressed onto the top end of the stairs, where they meet the tower, finishing the landing.

Parts-count warning: by my earlier records both lego-3710 plates (b45, b165) are already used, so no Plate 1x4 should be left. The unplaced list shows no reddish brown 1x4 plate either. One of my earlier identifications (for example b45 on page 14, or b165/b166 on page 49) is probably wrong. I recorded this piece as lego-3710 as the best match for the picture.

Step 24 (1x brick 2x4, 2x wedge): a light bluish gray 2x4 brick (b172) is placed on top of the long 1x6 beam b164 over the gate. Two light bluish gray wedged 2x2 facet bricks (b173, b174) go next to it on the same beam, making the roof of the gateway.
The wedge icon here matches lego-87620 (four are left in the unplaced list). The exact studs of b164 used by each piece are estimated, since b164 is only six studs long.

Step 25 (2x each): two light bluish gray 2x4 bricks (b175, b176) cover the top of the wall on each side of the gate roof, bridging the 1x4 tower brick and the 1x6 beam b164. Two Sand Green 1x1 bricks (b177, b178) are placed on the right tower and near the gate for colour accents.
The stud contacts are estimated from the picture. The Sand Green 1x1 count in the unplaced list may be out of step with my records; I used the colour shown in the picture.

Step 26: two light bluish gray 2x16 plates (b179, b180) are laid side by side along the top of the wall as the walkway. A light bluish gray 1x6 plate (b181) is then pressed on top, spanning both plates.

The stud contacts of the long plates are estimated: both are assumed to bridge the 2x4 bricks and the gate-roof bricks below. The 1x6 plate sits across the seam of the two long plates, so it clutches both.
Step 27: the first bricks of the parapet are added to the walkway: a 1x4 brick (b182) at the back left, a 1x2 brick (b183) next to it, and a masonry 1x2 brick (b184) near the right end.
I assumed the 1x4 and 1x2 sit on the back plate b179 and the masonry brick on the front plate b180. The picture is too small to read the positions closely.
Step 28: the back parapet of the walkway is extended with a light bluish gray 1x2 brick (b185), two wedged 2x2 facet bricks (b186, b187) and a masonry 1x2 brick (b188).

The two wedges match the last two lego-87620 in the unplaced list, and the masonry brick is the next-to-last lego-98283. I assumed the first three sit on the back plate b179 and the masonry brick on the front plate b180. This is estimated from the picture.

Step 29: four dark bluish gray jumper plates 1x2 (b189 to b192) are placed in the middle of the walkway, forming a dark patch where the archer will stand. Two dark bluish gray 45° 2x1 slopes with bottom pin (b193, b194) are added at the walkway corners: one at the front right and one at the back left.
The jumper plates are only drawn in the middle of the walkway. Which of the long plates each one covers is my estimate, since the middle ones probably cross the seam between b179 and b180.

Step 30 (2x jumper, 6x brick 1x2, 1x slope): the back parapet gets two dark jumper plates (b195, b196) at the back-left, six light bluish gray 1x2 bricks (b197 to b202) along the back and right parts, and a light bluish gray 30° 1x2 slope (b203) at the front right.
Which of the long plates each piece sits on is estimated. Four bricks are put on the back plate and two on the front plate, as the picture suggests. Please treat the splits as approximate.
Step 31 (6x): a light bluish gray 30° 1x2 slope is pressed on top of each of the six 1x2 parapet bricks placed on page 60 (b197 to b202), making the sloped crenellations of the wall.
The one-to-one pairing of slope and brick is my reading of the picture. The slopes cover the bricks' studs.

This page starts a new sub-assembly, the small swinging launcher mounted on a base. Step 1: the long tan pin goes into a black pin connector plate (b213). Step 2: the pin passes through the pin hole of the dark brown launcher (b211), which is the black-looking catapult piece in the picture. Step 3: the second pin connector plate (b214) closes the other end of the pin. Step 4: the two connector plates are pressed on the studs of a reddish brown 2x3 brick (b212).

The 'black' pieces in the pictures look black but I matched them to the unplaced list: the Launcher (lego-88289, Dark Brown) and the Technic Pin Connector Plates (lego-32530, Black). The reddish brown 2x3 brick (lego-3002) is recorded here as a new piece because I have not placed it before.
The launcher does not rest on any stud, since it swings on the pin between the two connector plates.

The launcher sub-assembly from page 62 (base b212) is placed on the walkway at the patch of dark jumper plates. No new pieces are added. The base b212 is now clutched to the jumper plates b189 to b192 and the walkway plates below, so I am adding that placement as a note rather than a new piece.

Because the schema only lets me list rests_on on newly placed pieces, I cannot add rests_on to b212, which was recorded on page 62 with an empty list. The intended contacts are: b212 rests on b189, b190, b191 and b192.

Step 33 (3x): three dark bluish gray round 1x1 bricks with open studs are placed on the front walkway plate b180 beside the launcher as ammunition. The picture shows two of them clearly, with the third assumed from the 3x box. The finger shows how the launcher is pushed to fire them, and the warning symbol says not to aim at faces.
Their exact studs on b180 are not specified. They are loose ammunition, so they simply sit on studs.

Step 34: a flagpole is built from a reddish brown cone (b218), a reddish brown 6L bar (b219) pushed into it, and two flags (b220 Pearl Gold, b221 Dark Green) slid onto the bar. The pole is then planted on the left tower, on the dark bluish gray round plate b169 at the top corner.
At the right tower top, a torch support (b222, Dark Brown, shown as black) is put on the green 1x1 brick b177. A trans-neon orange flame (b223) is pushed into it.

The page is shown from the front of the wall, so the model has been turned around. The positions on the towers are my reading: the flagpole at the left tower's top corner and the torch at the right tower's top.

Step 35 (2x): two black Technic pins with friction ridges (b224, b225) are pushed into the pin holes of the two Technic 1x2 bricks at the ends of the wall base (b103 on the left, b104 on the right). Only the left end is shown in the picture, and the right is assumed from the 2x box.
These pins are probably used later to hold extra pieces at the ends of the wall.

This page shows the finished bag 2 model: the Rohan wall with the archer standing on the walkway and the horse rider next to it. No new pieces are added. The minifigure bodies are not in the parts list.

Unplaced pieces still in the list: 4x lego-60474 round 4x4 plates, 1x lego-87079 tile 2x4 and 2x lego-98347 blades. They may be used on the following pages, for example the round plates under the wheels of the second set of models.
